caption: A 3x2 loop: observer O1 (1,0) watches O5 (2,0) and powers lamp L (0,0) behind it; O2 (0,1) watches L, O3 (1,1) watches O2, O4 (2,1) watches O3, O5 (2,0) watches O4. The lamp goes dark 4 gt after its power ends, so O2 sees two edges per pass.
Two observers face to face: each watches the other, so every output change of one is a shape update in front of the other. Kicked by placing the second observer (B) last.
Four observers in a horizontal square, each watching the previous one (A <- D <- C <- B <- A): one 2 gt pulse travels around, 2 gt per observer. Kicked by placing B last.

Torch + delay-1 repeater loop (draft, clk-rt): T (wall torch on A) -> 3 dust -> repeater R -> A. Inner loop period 4 * (1 + 1) = 8 gt: 7 x 8 = 56 <= 60, so the torch burns out at its 8th turn-off; R keeps T's input powered past that turn-off, so the 160 gt burnout re-check is not replaced by a relight tick, and T relights 160 gt after its 8th turn-off. Predicted period 220.

BURNOUT clock, 9 blocks (clk-rt): the 9-block torch + repeater loop with a delay-1 repeater. Inner loop period 8 (7 x 8 = 56 <= 60): the torch burns out at its 8th turn-off and relights 160 gt later (the repeater still powers it at that turn-off): period 4 + 56 + 160 = 220.

Comparator subtract clock, 8 blocks (draft, clk-rt): rear = redstone block (15); the output strongly powers block A; dust beside A carries A's strength to the comparator's side. Expected: output 15 / 1 alternating every 2 gt (period 4); the side dust 14 / 0.
Comparator subtract clock (draft, clk-rt): rear = redstone block (15), output -> 3 dust -> side. Expected: output alternates 15 / 2 every 2 gt (period 4), the last dust 13 / 0.

Torch + repeater loop, 9 blocks (draft, clk-rt): wall torch T on A -> repeater R reads T directly -> R strongly powers F -> dust beside F -> dust pointing into A. One inversion, loop delay 2 + 2d: period 4 (1 + d) = 12 with the delay-2 repeater (16 / 20 with delay 3 / 4).
C -> repeater(4) -> dust -> dust -> repeater(1) -> piston behind C: retraction at A+20, dist 1.

Self-starting: R is placed powered with no input; its turn-off is the first observer pulse. Calibrated sensor C strongly powers the stone below it; repeater R (delay 4) reads that stone; observer O (above R) watches R and plays note block N (diagonal to C: dist sqrt2, travel 1).
C -> repeater (4) -> stone X -> wall torch T on X's north face -> note block N diagonal to C.
Self-starting: R is placed powered with no input; its turn-off is the first observer pulse. Calibrated sensor C -> repeater R (delay 4) -> observer O watching R -> note block N (dist sqrt5).
Self-starting: calibrated C -> repeater R (delay 4, placed powered) -> observer O watching R -> note block N in line (dist 3 from C): event at A+20, travel 3.
Self-starting: fence gate E placed open+powered with no power closes on its placement update (BLOCK_CLOSE); then observer O's 3rd pulse on C opens it each period.
Self-starting: iron trapdoor placed open+powered with no power closes on its placement update.
Self-starting: piston placed extended (with its head) and unpowered retracts on its placement update (BLOCK_DEACTIVATE); then O's 3rd pulse on C moves it each period.

Self-starting 3-block clock: calibrated C, observer O watching C, oak trapdoor E behind O placed open+powered with no power: it closes on its placement update (BLOCK_CLOSE wakes C); then O's pulses at A+2, A+12, A+22 open/close E and only the A+22 one is heard (C re-arms at A+20).
Calibrated sensor C watched by observer O, note block N behind O (dist 2 from C).
Calibrated C, observer O watching C, piston E behind O (dist 2): O's 3rd pulse (A+22) extends E.
Calibrated C, observer O watching C, sticky piston E behind O (dist 2), facing away.
Calibrated C, observer O watching C, stone strongly powered by O, note block beyond it (dist 3).
C, observer O watching C, observer Q watching O (sideways), note block N behind Q (dist sqrt5): Q's 3rd pulse at A+24.
C, two observers in line, note block N (dist 3): 3rd pulse at A+24, travel 3.
C, three observers curling back (O watches C, Q watches O, R watches Q), note block N diagonal to C: A+26, travel 1.
Calibrated C, observer O watching C, EMPTY dispenser behind O: it fires 4 gt after each rising edge (empty dispense = BLOCK_ACTIVATE); the A+22 pulse fires it at A+26, heard at dist 2.
Plain sensor C (30 active + 10 cooldown), observer O watching C, note block behind O (dist 2): O's pulse after C's COOLDOWN->INACTIVE (A+42) plays the note.
Plain sensor C, observer O watching C, empty dispenser behind O (fires 4 gt after O's A+42 pulse).

Pure vibration ring (nothing but sensors changes state): calibrated sensors S1 (1,0,0), S2 (15,0,8), S3 (1,0,16), each with an amethyst block beside it; when S_i activates its amethyst resonates and S_(i+1) hears it floor(dist) = 15 gt later. P = 3 x 15. A1 is out of S3's range (dist^2 257), so after the kick only S2 wakes; afterwards the sensor two hops ahead is always still in its 20 gt dead time. Kick: right-click the note block K (only S1 is within 16 of it; S1 faces east so its back, K, gets no power from it).

Hopper slosh, 4 blocks (clk-item): two hoppers facing each other hold one item; it hops back and forth, 7 gt per hop (the receiving hopper was empty: TransferCooldown 8 - 1). A comparator reading the west hopper is on 7 gt, off 7 gt. redsim: P=14 gt, warmup 3, family comparator+hopper, 4 blocks, output on 7/14 gt, 1 rising edge(s)

Ring lock, 10 blocks (clk-item): 8 hoppers around a 3x3 square with a comparator in the middle that reads the west hopper and points into the east one, locking it whenever the west one holds an item; 4 swords. The lock makes the items queue and overtake: period 15 gt. redsim: P=15 gt, warmup 122, family comparator+hopper, 10 blocks, output on 7/15 gt, 1 rising edge(s)

Ring lock, 10 blocks (clk-item): 8 hoppers around a 3x3 square, a comparator in the middle reads the west hopper and locks the east one (it points into it); 3 items (2 stone + 1 sword). Items queue at the locked hopper and are released in an irregular order: the whole pattern repeats only every 654 gt. redsim: P=654 gt, warmup 22, family comparator+hopper, 10 blocks, output on 234/654 gt, 30 rising edge(s)

Dropper ring, 10 blocks (clk-item): hoppers and droppers around a 3x3 square, each passing items to the next; a comparator in the middle reads one ring container and points into the opposite one, a dropper: each time an item arrives under the comparator, the dropper fires 4 gt later (rising edge) and pushes one item on. Items wait in the droppers for a trigger, so the cycle is not a multiple of 7: 20 gt. redsim: P=20 gt, warmup 34, family comparator+dropper+hopper, 10 blocks, output on 7/20 gt, 1 rising edge(s)

Comparator COUNTER clock (clk-rt): an inner comparator fading ring (3 + 3 compare comparators, one level lost per lap, a wall torch refills it) whose refill pulse, turned into strength 1 by a subtract comparator (side = 14 from a redstone block + 2 dust), decrements a LOSSLESS comparator ring (3 + 3 comparators, one in subtract mode) by exactly one level; when the counter is empty its own torch refills it: period = about 14 inner periods

Comparator COUNTER clock (clk-rt): an inner comparator fading ring (4 + 4 compare comparators, one level lost per lap, a wall torch refills it) whose refill pulse, turned into strength 1 by a subtract comparator (side = 14 from a redstone block + 2 dust), decrements a LOSSLESS comparator ring (4 + 4 comparators, one in subtract mode) by exactly one level; when the counter is empty its own torch refills it: period = about 14 inner periods

Comparator COUNTER clock (clk-rt): an inner comparator fading ring (6 + 6 compare comparators, one level lost per lap, a wall torch refills it) whose refill pulse, turned into strength 1 by a subtract comparator (side = 14 from a redstone block + 2 dust), decrements a LOSSLESS comparator ring (6 + 6 comparators, one in subtract mode) by exactly one level; when the counter is empty its own torch refills it: period = about 14 inner periods

Dropper ring with a delayed fire (clock item sweep-dropring --delays): a hopper ring 4 or 5 deep with 1 or 2 droppers in the bottom row; the comparator in the inner column reads the top-row hopper above it and fires the dropper at the bottom through 1 or 2 repeaters (each on stone). Two stones: one waits in a dropper until the other passes the read hopper; the repeater delays (2 gt each step) shift the period off the multiples of 7, so ring size x dropper count x delays reach every P from 42 up (and 29-40 odd/even below). Here P = 29. redsim: P=29 gt, warmup 38, family comparator+dropper+hopper+repeater, 14 blocks, output on 7/29 gt, 1 rising edge(s)

Census find (3x1x2, k<=5): a calibrated sensor and a plain sensor side by side, two observers (one watching the calibrated sensor, one watching that observer) and a note block: the calibrated sensor's own observer loop runs every 26 gt and the plain sensor, hearing the same note at most once per 40 gt, repeats every 130 gt = 5 loops (output: the plain sensor).

Census find (3x1x2, k<=5): two sensors and two empty dispensers: an observer on the calibrated sensor fires one dispenser, the other sits by the plain sensor; each sensor hears the dispensers at most once per dead time and gates the dispenser it powers; the joint cycle repeats every 135 gt (output: a full-period sensor).

Census find (4x1x2, k<=4): two sensors and one dispenser. A calibrated sensor watched by an observer that fires an empty dispenser runs its own 28 gt loop (the c28 clock); the plain sensor behind it hears the same dispenser at most once per 40 gt dead time (its power into the calibrated sensor's back is a frequency filter at 10, the dispenser's own frequency, so the loop keeps running): the plain sensor's cycle repeats every 140 gt = 5 loops (output: the plain sensor).

Ring lock 3 x 20, item-count tuned (clk-item): the ring lock of 42 hoppers with 5 + n stones in the corner hopper: each stone adds one 8-gt hopper move to the queue in front of the locked hopper, P = 7 L + 8 N - 34, up to N = 33 (P 524).

Hopper pair with a delayed lock (clk-item): 2 swords start in the west-facing hopper B; the comparator reading the east-facing hopper A powers a stone, the dust beside it feeds a repeater (delay n + 1) pointing into B, which locks B from 2 + 2 (n + 1) gt after A gets a sword until that long after it empties: P = 9 + 2 (n + 1). Delay 4 gives 25 (the lock misses a move).

Ring lock 3 x 6, item-count tuned (clk-item): the ring lock of 14 hoppers with 5 + n stones in the corner hopper: each stone adds one 8-gt hopper move to the queue in front of the locked hopper, P = 7 L + 8 N - 34, up to N = floor((7 L - 2) / 8) - 3 = 9.

Powder snow dispenser with a repeater (clk-item): a dispenser facing down holds a powder snow bucket; each fire toggles the cell under it (place / pick up); an observer watching that cell pulses into a stone whose dust feeds a repeater (delay n + 1) on the observer pointing into the dispenser: P = 2 x (2 + 2 (n + 1) + 4). Digital P=8 hopper pair (clk-item): the analog pair (3 swords, cooldowns 5 apart: the east-facing hopper A holds 1 or 2 swords, strength 3 or 6) read by a SUBTRACT comparator whose side input is a constant 3 from a second comparator reading a dead-end hopper holding one sword (facing down into air, it never moves): output max(s(A) - 3, 0) = 0 or 3, digital, P = 8.

Digital P=24, 2x2 hopper ring with mixed items (clk-item): 4 hoppers in a ring holding 2 swords and 2 stones (in another arrangement than the P=16 one); the reader is a SUBTRACT comparator whose side input is a constant 1 (a second comparator reading a dead-end hopper holding one stone): output max(s - 1, 0) = 2 (a sword passes) or 0 (a stone), digital, P = 24.

A calibrated sculk sensor, a straight line of n delay-4 repeaters read from it, an observer watching the last one and a note block behind it: the line's turn-on plays the note 8n+2 gt after the sensor fires and the vibration travels n+2 gt back (n <= 14 keeps the note within 16). Self-starting: the repeaters are placed powered. P = 4 + 9n gt, 3 + 2n blocks (n = 3: P 31, 9 blocks). Built by `mctas clock sculk family replin --n 3`.

A calibrated sculk sensor, n delay-4 repeaters out, a two-dust U-turn, n repeaters back, an observer beside the sensor watching the last one and a note block diagonal to the sensor: the note plays 16n+2 gt after the sensor fires and is heard 1 gt later, for any n. Self-starting. P = 3 + 16n gt, 7 + 4n blocks (n = 2: P 35, 15 blocks). Built by `mctas clock sculk family hairpin --n 2`.

The hairpin with a plain sculk sensor (re-armed 40 gt after firing, so n >= 3): n delay-4 repeaters out, a two-dust U-turn, n back, an observer and a note block next to the sensor. Self-starting. P = 3 + 16n gt, 7 + 4n blocks (n = 3: P 51, 19 blocks). Built by `mctas clock sculk family hairpin-plain --n 3`.

A pure vibration racetrack: calibrated sculk sensors on two straight lines 18 apart (17 between sensors: hop 16) joined by a turn sensor at each end (hops 15); each sensor's resonator (amethyst; the first a note block, right-clicked as the kick) rings when it fires and only the next sensor is within 16. P = 28 + 32n gt, 4 + 4n blocks (n = 1: P 60, 8 blocks). Built by `mctas clock sculk family racetrack --n 1`.

The racetrack with plain sculk sensors (radius 8, deaf 40 gt): lines 10 apart, 9 between sensors (hop 8), turn sensors 6 out (hops 7); m >= 3 so the next sensor has re-armed. P = 12 + 16n gt, 4 + 4n blocks (n = 3: P 60, 16 blocks). Built by `mctas clock sculk family racetrack-plain --n 3`.

Latch hopper clock, item-count tuned (clk-item): two hoppers facing each other pass N = n + 2 stones from one to the other and back, one per 8 gt; a waxed copper bulb remembers the direction: the comparators reading the hoppers light a torch when their hopper is EMPTY, and those torches (one under the bulb, one under a stone beside it) toggle the bulb when the source runs dry; a comparator reading the bulb lights a dust on the stone above hopper A (locks A) and that stone's wall torch locks hopper B when the bulb is off. P = 16 N - 2 gt with 17 blocks: up to 5118 gt (4.3 min) with 320 stones.

Extendable family clk-misc-crafter-loop (n = 0): P = 91 + 28n = 91 gt, 7 + 2n = 7 blocks. A crafter crafts back and forth between 1 slime block and 9 slime balls; 1 hopper(s) carry each result back into it (one item per 8 gt). A comparator reads the hopper that feeds the crafter through a stone and two observers pulse the crafter on both of its edges: when that hopper empties the crafter holds a whole recipe and crafts 4 gt later; when it fills, the crafter is empty or partly filled and nothing matches. Extension: 2 more hoppers (+28 gt: the block and the 9 balls each cross 2 more hoppers).

A daylight detector clock: an inverted daylight detector reads 0 under the open sky and 1 when a block hides the sky right above it (sky light 14 from the sides). It updates only when the game time is a multiple of 20 gt. An observer on it pulses a sticky piston (through the stone under the piston) for 2 gt: a 2 gt pulse makes a sticky piston spit the block in front of it one cell further (here: over the detector) and the next pulse pull it back (the block 2 cells away is no longer moving). So every detector update toggles the cover and the next update (20 gt later) sees the change: P = 40 gt.

A water clock: a walled channel on a stone floor between two water sources, 5 cells apart. The cell F2 two steps from the left source holds flowing water of level 2 (fed from the left) or level 3 (fed from the right when the left feed is cut): an observer in the wall watches it, and through the stone behind it pulses a sticky piston for 2 gt. Each pulse toggles the piston's block between the wall and the channel cell F1 next to the left source (a 2 gt pulse spits the block one cell further; the next pulse pulls it back). Cutting or reopening F1 changes F2's level a few water ticks (5 gt) later.

When the log leaves, the distances count up to 7 and the last leaf changes once more.
